# `Q-22-13` — Math Syntax Error

> The math expression contains a construct the parser could not interpret: an alignment `&` outside an environment, a stray `\begin`/`\end`, or another malformed piece of syntax.

## What this means

This is the catch-all for malformed math that does not fit a more specific code. The offending piece is underlined; the expression is emitted verbatim in formats that need a conversion.

## Why this happens

Common causes: an `&` used as an ordinary character (write `\&`), `\\` or `&` outside an `aligned`/`matrix` environment, or the remains of an incomplete edit.

## How to fix it

Check the underlined text against the LaTeX math syntax you intended.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
